speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To begin our evaluation of your chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of camping and a fellow camper becoming ill is concerning for a parasitic infection like Giardia. Given the relief from defecation and the feeling of incomplete evacuation, could you describe the specific nature of your abdominal pain and whether you have experienced significant weight loss or night sweats?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Ulcerative Colitis)

The negative inflammatory markers (CRP) and stool studies make an acute infectious etiology like Giardia or C. Diff unlikely. Given your four-month history of bloody/mucousy stools with urgency and incomplete evacuation, your symptoms are classic for ulcerative colitis. Do you have a family history of inflammatory bowel disease, and have you noticed any joint pain or skin rashes?
